findings.finding: pull_frame rescales broker microsecond PTS back to packet_timebase, sets frame.pts and best_effort_timestamp, initializes pkt_dts unknown, then searches256 timing slots by exact original packet PTS to copy duration/DTS/position/key flag.
The public receive path unconditionally assigns best_effort_timestamp=guess_correct_pts(frame.pts,frame.pkt_dts) after the codec callback succeeds. The wrapper preassignment does not bypass this.

guess_correct_pts counts non-increasing PTS and DTS separately and prefers a known PTS while faultyPTS<=faultyDTS or DTS is unknown. Strictly increasing output PTS therefore remain selected even when source-packet DTS becomes nonmonotonic after presentation reordering.

pkt_dts is documented as DTS copied from the packet that triggered returning a frame, also providing presentation time inferred from DTS alone. Copying the originating packet DTS by PTS match is not generally identical to this native output-time packet semantics for Bframes.

SETS_FRAME_PROPS suppresses packet-property auto-copy, not best-effort timestamp guessing. SETS_PKT_DTS only guards the simple decode callback assignment in this source; adding that flag to this receive_frame codec would not change the observed final guessing path.

Only software fallback updates has_b_frames. Hardware leaves the caller/default value. The inspected core reference to has_b_frames is a pkt_pos convenience in the legacy simple decode callback; the receive_frame path does not use it to reorder frames or timestamps.

Frame duration is copied only on an exact timing-table PTS match; a miss leaves0(unknown) and fill_frame_props does not infer a video duration. Firefox microsecond packet timestamps use AV_TIME_BASE_Q fallback and should roundtrip exactly; duplicate/unknown PTS, over256 outstanding timings or sub-microsecond external time bases require separate handling.

existing_test_gap.finding: The seven-packet Firefox DTS test uses an immediate-return stub, preserving decode-order nonmonotonic PTS rather than emitting presentation order. It verifies pts,pkt_dts,duration and unchanged input packets, but not best_effort_timestamp. It cannot establish the real reordered-frame best-effort behavior.

algorithm_walkthrough.scope: Python arithmetic walkthrough of the inspected comparison logic; not an execution of the candidate library or a board trace.

current_conclusion: There is a real distinction between source-packet DTS and native output pkt_dts semantics, and the existing test does not cover final best_effort. Neither proves the current60fps drops. To identify a timestamp cause, correlate actual returned frame pts/best_effort/pkt_dts/duration with the Firefox-selected presentation time and deadline. Keep decode throughput, presentation counters and physical display output separate.
